meta.title: H.O.M.E. — The Disappearing Home
meta.description: When the forest burns, who loses their home? A storybook for Kalimantan's wildlife, and for the neighbors who breathe the smoke.
meta.tagline: When the forest burns, who loses their home?

story.cover_subtitle: A painted forest in Kalimantan, Borneo.
story.meet_intro: Every tree is a bed. Every river is a road. Every leaf is a story.
story.tuki_desc: Tuki is a young Bornean orangutan. Each night Tuki builds a new nest from fresh leaves. Each morning Tuki watches the mist lift through the canopy. This is the only home Tuki knows.
story.liku_desc: Liku is a Sunda pangolin. Liku walks the forest floor after dark, listening for termites under the roots. The scales are a shield. They are not a shelter from fire.
story.madu_desc: Madu is a sun bear. Madu looks for bees in high branches and leaves claw marks on bark, like a diary.
story.kecil_desc: Kecil is a lesser mouse deer, no bigger than a hare. Kecil steps through the undergrowth like a whisper.
story.rangkong_desc: Rangkong is a helmeted hornbill. The call carries through the canopy at dawn. The same nest tree can matter for years.
story.fire_text: It starts as a glow on the horizon. The air thickens. The colors thin.
story.fire_text2: Satellite sensors record thermal anomalies across Kalimantan. A bright point is a place where a home may be at risk. It is not proof that a forest has burned, and it is not proof that an animal died.
story.evidence_title: The evidence stays in separate rows.
story.evidence_text: These are satellite fire detections in the loaded snapshot. A detection is a thermal anomaly. It is not, by itself, a wildlife impact.
story.reach_title: The smoke does not stop at the river.
story.reach_text: West and Central Kalimantan share an airshed with Sarawak, Sabah, and Brunei. In the southwest monsoon, that smoke has also crossed the sea to Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore. Schools have closed. Flights have waited. People have struggled to breathe. The fire is local. The harm can be national, next door.
story.choice_text: The forest cannot wait. It does not have to disappear.
story.return_text: When someone acts, the ending can change. The paint is still wet. This home can still be helped.
story.proof_text: Every dataset on this site names its source. Every claim keeps its evidence level.

transparency.title: Data transparency
transparency.subtitle: Every dataset has a source. Every source has a license.
claims: We do not claim a fire detection proves an animal died.
We do not predict where an animal will move.
We do not treat a species range as presence at a coordinate.
We do not process donations. Giving is handled by the partner you choose.
We do not treat a protected area as a guarantee of safety.
We do not treat a model score, an NDVI drop, or a neighbor-country count as a health tally or a mortality tally.

reach.title: The smoke keeps the address.
reach.lede: A fire in Kalimantan can become a week of closed windows in another country.
reach.body: H.O.M.E. is the habitat of our missing endangered. The story starts with Tuki's trees. It does not end at the border. Malaysia, Brunei, and Singapore share the air. On the same island, Sarawak, Sabah, and Brunei can live with smoke from a peat fire that started in Kalimantan. Across the sea, the southwest monsoon has carried that smoke to Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore. In severe seasons, schools have closed, flights have waited, and people have struggled to breathe. That reach can be massive. This page does not turn it into a death count.
reach.neighbors_body: Counts below are detections in this snapshot that sit in West and Central Kalimantan, or south of 1°N. They mark a shared airshed and a known seasonal pathway. They are not a smoke forecast, and they are not a count of illness.
reach.sdg_body: Six goals meet in one fire season. Tiles use the official numbers and colors. The drawings are original, so they are not the United Nations icon set.
reach.models_body: Python runs offline over every snapshot: fires, burned area, occurrences, protected areas, species, and the NDVI workbook. The browser only shows the JSON. Nothing here predicts where an animal will walk, or whether one died.
